To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the mechanisms of bacterial colonization of the respiratory tract are conserved among many different species and that these mechanisms are important for the development of bacterial infections.

bacterial colonization of the respiratory tract is a complex process that is dependent on a range of factors including the ability to adhere to host cells, to evade host immunity, to grow under nutrient limited conditions, to be transmitted to a new host and to cause disease.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms that underlie the ability of bacterial pathogens to cause respiratory tract infections.
understanding the mechanisms of colonization of bacteria that cause disease in humans.
the molecular basis of bacterial colonization of the respiratory tract and how it influences the pathogenesis of disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
bacterial respiratory tract colonization is a complex and dynamic process, which is influenced by both the host and the bacterium.
colonization of the respiratory tract by bacteria requires a complex set of interactions between host and pathogen that are still poorly understood.
colonization is a prerequisite to infection, and the mechanisms that enable colonization are also those that enable infection and disease.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the mechanisms that underlie bacterial colonization of the respiratory tract are conserved among a range of opportunistic pathogens.
the mechanisms that allow bacteria to colonize the respiratory tract are conserved across a range of pathogens.
the colonization of the upper respiratory tract is the key step for the development of lower respiratory tract infections, which is the most common cause of morbidity worldwide.
The main takeaway from our work is that
colonization is a prerequisite for all lower respiratory tract infections and, thus, a key target for prevention.
colonization is a complex process involving multiple bacterial traits.
colonization and pathogenesis are not separate processes.
